key_insight: Bayesian inference fused with photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade—separating interface, bulk, and transport-layer contributions over time.
engineering_relevance: This enables more targeted durability engineering by identifying the specific interfaces or regions that need passivation or materials changes to improve solar-cell stability.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated devices
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to Bayesian parameter inference
Time-lapse tracking of inferred optoelectronic parameter maps during aging
evidence_signal: Under 70 °C full-spectrum light aging, the inferred maps showed strong spatial heterogeneity and allowed the authors to distinguish degradation at hole/electron transport interfaces versus the bulk.
watch_item: The inferred degradation origin depends on model assumptions and imaging/model quality, so careful calibration and validation are needed before generalizing to other device stacks or aging conditions.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
